translation_notes: prefixes: RDFS->rdfs (OWL and RDF are imported but only RDF.type is used, written `a`).

Runs on the REAL semantikon 1.4.4: original.py gains one import line (`from semantikon.ontology import SNS, _get_bound_graph, _to_owl_restriction, _translate_triples`) for the names the region's own file defines; the driver builds a real SemantikonDiGraph with real Node/Input/Output. No shim, nothing re-implemented.

Ten `g.add` calls become four `+{ }` after `@graph g` (written once `g = _get_bound_graph()` is assigned; `g += ...` is in place, so g is never rebound). Subjects are shared within each block (`;`). Python str values (port, labels) are interpolated bare; `Literal(data["value"])` and `Literal(data["hash"])` are kept inside the interpolation because `value` is any runtime value and the coercion policy is not Literal(x) for every type.

The existence test `g.value(data_node, SNS.has_value) is None` becomes `not m{ {data_node} {SNS.has_value} ?v }` (receiver-less, current graph g): the code only asks 'is there a value?', so bool, not .first(). The three `g += _to_owl_restriction(...)`/`_translate_triples(...)` stay as they are (they return Graphs).

Property of the original worth knowing: `g` is fresh in this function, so the guard is true unless the region itself has just written (data_node, has_value, _) through the caller's `has_specified_io` argument. Real callers pass SNS.has_participant / has_output-like predicates, so the guard is effectively always true there; the driver reaches the false branch with has_specified_io=SNS.has_value and node == data_node.

Proof: 8 calls (a-box with value+hash; guard-false case; neighbour (node has_value data_node) with node != data_node; no value; triples + derived_from with the append to data['triples']; t-box with and without hash; a flat triple). The original returns graphs of 5-12 triples and its has_value triple is present or absent depending on the guard. Mutants all FAIL: guard inverted (4 calls), subject unbound (call 2), object bound instead of subject (call 2), predicate unbound (3 calls); restored OK.
